mina: hitting a weird edge in the C# SDK quickstart: when a long SSE stream is interrupted by auth rotation, resumed chunks sometimes produce mojibake / duplicated characters. Seems like multibyte UTF-8 sequences are being split across the reconnect boundary and the decoder ends up emitting replacement chars or doubled text.

eric: interesting. are you seeing actual corrupted bytes on the wire or is this the client-side decoder reassembling incorrectly?

mina: captured bytes from proxy: the original chunk ended with the first two bytes of a 3-byte UTF-8 sequence, then reconnect resumes and sends remaining byte plus next event. Raw fragments: 
```
chunk A: "data: Hello \xE3\x81"
chunk B (resume): "\x82
data: world

"
```
If the client decodes A on receive it emits replacement char for the incomplete sequence; later when B arrives the decoder re-decodes and we see both replacement char and correct character, leading to a duplicated/garbled output.

zhou: C# StreamReader/Decoder handles partial sequences if you keep the Decoder state between reads. But if on reconnect we create a fresh reader/decoder (new network stream) we lose decoder state. On resume with Last-Event-ID we should either: 1) discard any partial trailing bytes before reconnecting (so we don't emit replacement chars for incomplete sequences), or 2) buffer and re-decode together with the resumed bytes.

eric: but buffering across reconnect can duplicate content if server re-sends overlapping bytes. We need to dedupe by event id too. So rule: on reconnect with Last-Event-ID=X, drop partial UTF-8 bytes retained by decoder, then resume and dedupe by id <= X. That avoids both replacement chars and duplicates.

mina: implemented a local workaround: keep Decoder state until we see a blank-line terminator; if reconnect is needed mid-codepoint, drop decoder state and discard the pending incomplete char. Not ideal semantically but avoids duplicate mojibake.

sdk-bot: note: sdk/csharp v0.9.2-alpha includes an experimental fix for streaming decoder state handling on resume. Please test under 50-client stress harness.

zhou: one more complication: some proxies normalize line endings, others may split at CRLF boundaries; we should normalize incoming bytes (convert CRLF -> LF) before feeding decoder so we don't split multibyte sequences at CRLF boundaries unpredictably.

eric: add tests: (1) artificial split of multibyte sequences across reconnect, (2) resume with overlapping bytes + id dedupe, (3) race where two reconnects deliver overlapping but out-of-order chunks.

mina: filed GH issue and attached repro harness (small C# console app + tcp-proxy that can split/merge chunks). PR incoming with decoder-drop-on-resume + id-filter.
